title: MgF2/HfO2 chirped mirror stack for broadband rejection
scientific_hypothesis: A chirped multilayer stack using MgF2 and HfO2 with gradually varying layer thicknesses will achieve broader stopband coverage across 300-1100 nm compared to a periodic stack, while maintaining acceptable transmission in 255-280 nm.
design_principle: Chirped mirrors vary the optical thickness of successive layers to broaden the reflection band. Higher index contrast (HfO2 vs MgF2) increases reflectivity per interface, reducing the number of layers needed for a given stopband depth. The chirp profile can be optimized to cover both visible and NIR stopbands simultaneously.
design_variables: individual layer thicknesses for all 20 film layers with chirp constraint
chirp rate parameter implicit in thickness progression
manufacturing_considerations: HfO2 may have higher UV absorption than Al2O3, requiring verification
Chirped profiles require precise thickness control during deposition
theory_basis: Chirped mirror design for broadband reflection
High index contrast for enhanced stopband depth
Transfer matrix method with non-periodic layer sequences
expected_advantages: Higher index contrast than MgF2/Al2O3 enables fewer layers for same rejection
Chirped profile can cover both visible and NIR stopbands in one structure
No defect cavity simplifies the topology
known_risks: HfO2 absorption edge may be near 255 nm, reducing passband transmission
Chirped optimization is more complex than periodic stack tuning
May require more layers than periodic design to achieve same passband sharpness
execution_request_english: Design a chirped mirror bandpass filter on fused silica substrate. Stack topology: air incident medium, then 10 repeated pairs of MgF2 (Rodriguez-de_Marcos) and hfo2 (MgF2 (Rodriguez-de_Marcos) first from air side) with chirped thickness profile, terminating on SiO2 (Gao) substrate. Total film layers: 20. All 20 layer thicknesses are optimizable design variables without requiring strict periodicity. Wavelength bands: maximize transmittance in 255-280 nm, minimize transmittance in 300-700 nm and 700-1100 nm. No metal layers. Normal incidence, unpolarized light. Total layers must not exceed 30.
